editorial:
Imagine you and your three best friends are heading home after a wild weekend at a cookoff in Texas. You decide to take a detour to visit Marfa, a town famous for weird ghost lights that no one can explain. You get the feeling of a classic road trip movie where things start out fun and relaxed, but the vibe quickly shifts into something much stranger. The movie does a great job of making you feel like you are right there in the car with these friends, wondering if those lights in the distance are just a trick of the eye or something from another world.

You will notice that the chemistry between the actors feels real, which makes the scary parts hit harder. While the story starts a bit slow, the twists in the second half really pick up the speed. It is not a huge budget film, but it uses the empty Texas landscape to create a creepy mood.
endingExplained: You find out that the mysterious lights are actually tied to aliens who are experimenting on humans. In the final scenes, the group realizes they are trapped in a loop or a game. Most of the friends do not make it out alive as the aliens reveal their true plan. The movie wraps up with a shocking twist showing that the world they thought they were in was not real, leaving you wondering if anyone actually escaped.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves low budget sci-fi and mystery movies.
